# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Please do not open a public issue for a security problem.**

Use GitHub's private reporting instead: go to the **Security** tab of this repository and choose
**Report a vulnerability**. That opens a private advisory visible only to the maintainers, and it
lets us work on a fix and publish it together with the disclosure.

What helps, in rough order of usefulness:

 - what an attacker gains - crash the device, make it misbehave, read something it should not;
 - the shortest input that triggers it. A frame capture or a byte sequence is worth far more than
   a description of one;
 - which module and which version or commit;
 - whether it needs a live link to a SINTRAN machine, or just bytes on the transport.

You will get an acknowledgement. This is a small project maintained in spare time, so please do not
read a slow reply as a lack of interest - if a week passes with no word, send a reminder through the
same advisory.

## What is in scope

Everything under `src/`: the HDLC byte framer, the LAPB link layer, the XMSG datagram layer, the
XROUT letter builder, the TAD terminal session, and the COSMOS file-access and FTP components when
they are compiled in. All of it parses bytes that arrive from a serial line or a TCP socket, so a
frame that makes the library read or write outside a buffer is exactly what we want to hear about.

## What is not in scope

 - **The age of the protocols themselves.** LAPB, XMSG, TAD and COSMOS file access have no
   authentication worth the name, no encryption and no integrity checking beyond a 16-bit frame
   check. That is what they were; reproducing them faithfully is the purpose of this library, not
   a defect. Do not run any of it on a network you do not control, and do not expose the FTP
   component to the internet.
 - A report generated by a scanner with no demonstration that the finding is reachable.
 - Denial of service by sending an unreasonable volume of traffic.
 - Anything requiring the attacker to already be able to run code on the device.

## Supported versions

There are no tagged releases yet, so the **default branch is what is supported**. Once releases
begin, the most recent one will be.

## Credit

Unless you ask otherwise, you will be named in the advisory and in the release notes for the fix.
